title: Digital Tachometer & Speed Trap
tagline: Precision lab instrumentation: measure motor RPM using optical photogates and magnetic Hall effect sensors with hardware interrupts!

phases.instructions: Locate from your kit: Arduino Uno, Photo Interrupter Photogate (comp_05), 3144 Hall Effect Sensor (comp_38), 7-Segment Display (comp_32), 74HC595 Shift Register, 130 DC Motor (comp_33), Neodymium magnet, Breadboard, and wires.
verificationCheckpoints: ITR9608 photogate slotted optical switch ready

phases.instructions: Connect Photogate OUT to Pin 2 (Hardware Interrupt 0). Connect Hall Sensor OUT to Pin 3 (Hardware Interrupt 1). Connect 74HC595 Latch/Clock/Data to Pins 4, 5, 6. Connect Shift Register outputs to 7-Segment segments A-G.
verificationCheckpoints: Photogate and Hall sensors wired to hardware interrupt pins (Pins 2 and 3)

phases.instructions: Pass a piece of cardboard through the photogate slot: observe digital signal drop on Pin 2. Wave magnet near Hall sensor: observe digital signal drop on Pin 3.
verificationCheckpoints: Optical beam break triggers clean falling edge
Magnetic field triggers clean falling edge

phases.instructions: Review hardware interrupt velocity math: ISR increments a pulse counter. Every 500ms, the main loop computes RPM = (pulses * 60000) / (timeDelta * slots) and shifts digits out to the 7-segment display.
phases.codeExplanation:
- attachInterrupt() executes countPulse() instantly when a slot breaks the optical beam without polling delay.
- volatile keyword ensures the compiler doesn't optimize away the interrupt-modified variable.
- Periodic calculation window converts pulse frequency into engineering units (RPM).
verificationCheckpoints: Understand atomic variable access during time window calculation

phases.instructions: Upload sketch. Power up DC motor with slotted disc spinning in the photogate slot. Observe precise, jitter-free RPM readings updating live!
verificationCheckpoints: RPM scales smoothly with motor voltage

phases.instructions: Tachometer Instrument Specialist! You harnessed hardware interrupts to measure high-speed physical velocity.
verificationCheckpoints: Ready to claim Tachometer Tech badge

variants.title: Optical Slotted Photogate
variants.description: Use ITR9608 slotted optical gate instead of magnetic Hall sensor for detecting gear tooth passes.
variants.wiringDifferences: Connect photogate digital output to Pin 2 interrupt

extensionMissions.title: Overspeed Governor Interlock
extensionMissions.objective: Trip a safety relay to cut motor power if rotational speed exceeds 3,000 RPM.
hints: If triggered, drive relay pin LOW and latch fault state

story: How fast is that motor really spinning? Build laboratory instrumentation! Combine an optical slotted photogate and a magnetic Hall effect sensor with hardware interrupts to calculate rotational velocity in Revolutions Per Minute (RPM) and display on a 7-segment display.

troubleshooting.symptom: RPM reads zero even when motor is spinning
troubleshooting.cause: Sensor connected to non-interrupt pin, or slotted disc not passing between photogate posts
troubleshooting.solution: Verify sensor output is wired strictly to digital Pin 2 (Interrupt 0) or Pin 3 (Interrupt 1).
diagnosticSteps: Test countPulse() by manually tapping Pin 2 to GND
